Instead, the investigation went in a different direction: it did attempt to diagnose the cause of the latency swings directly, concluding that latency is driven by long output generations (more output tokens = more latency, ~10ms/token constant) and a shift in model mix (more sonnet-5 traffic diluting the account-wide average). While it does list some gaps (no time-to-first-token for sonnet-5, no X-Ray tracing, calls not attributable to app/feature), these are presented as secondary limitations alongside a confident causal diagnosis, not as the primary conclusion that telemetry is insufficient to diagnose the incident. The investigation explicitly provides a root cause for the latency (workload/token volume and model mix), rather concluding that there isn't enough telemetry and explaining why.

This is a fundamentally different framing from the expected answer, which centers on telemetry-gap diagnosis (LLM-TEL-001/002/003) as the root cause/conclusion itself, not as a side gap. The actual investigation's Cause findings focus on output-length-driven latency and model-mix shift, not on telemetry inadequacy as the core finding.
